item.title: Dakar 2026 Youth Olympics opens in historic first for Africa
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01
Dakar 2026 Youth Olympics opens in historic first for Africa Photo shows the Olympic rings during the opening ceremony of the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal, Oct. 31, 2026. (Xinhua/Chen Wei) DAKAR, Oct. 31 (Xinhua) -- The Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games (YOG) opened on Saturday, marking the first time an Olympic event has been held on African soil. The opening ceremony took place at the 55,000-seat Abdoulaye Wade Stadium in Diamniadio, a new city located 30 km from Senegal's capital of Dakar. According to the organizing committee, Khady Niang, the ceremony director, said the show allows Africa to "tell the world who we are, where we come from and where we want to go." The two-hour show started at 6:30 p.m. local time, marked by the arrival of International Olympic Committee President Kirsty Coventry and Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye. Following the parade of athletes, the spotlight turned to a story of three generations passing the baton from one to the next: Alkebulan, the mother, represented the values of ancestral Africa; her son, Keb, embodied Africa today; and Sitoe, a young Senegalese girl, symbolized hope for the future. The opening act paid tribute to the Africa of the past, immediately electrifying the crowd as Alkebulan rode into the arena on horseback. Iconic instruments, including the sabar, the tama (talking drum) and the djembe, introduced the continent's rich musical heritage, while traditional attire from Mali, Ghana, Senegal and South Africa showcased the diversity of African cultural traditions. The momentum built with performances of Senegal's traditional faux-lion dance and wrestlers' dance, culminating in a finale in which 360 dancers came together to form the map of Africa. In the second act, Keb arrived on a motorcycle in a scene inspired by the Senegalese film Touki Bouki. He led Sitoe and the spectators into the world of contemporary African art, striking a chord with younger generations. As Keb and Sitoe strolled through the streets, a series of artistic performances featuring live painting, music, dance and hip-hop brought the scene to life. The festivities were followed by the parade of flags representing the participating national Olympic committees, with Greece and the Refugee Olympic Team leading the procession and host nation Senegal bringing up the rear. "For years, we have been talking about this moment -- the first Olympic sporting event on African soil and now here we are. This historic moment is for Senegal, for Africa, for our entire Olympic movement, and to all of our young amazing athletes," Coventry said in her speech. "This is the Africa that I am so proud and so excited for the world to experience," she added, voicing hope for young talents to "believe in yourselves, to dream big and to do things you never thought were possible." After Senegalese President Faye officially declared the fourth Summer Youth Olympic Games open, the stadium erupted in vibrant Afrobeats music. The celebration continued with sports demonstrations, a choreographed formation of the Olympic rings and the Dakar 2026 emblem, the Olympic anthem, the raising of the Olympic flag and the solemn reading of the Youth Olympic oath. The much-anticipated lighting of the Olympic cauldron came last. Senegalese fencer Abdourahmane Marieme Sy, 17, and judoka Aicha Diop, 15, jointly carried the final torch, receiving the flame from canoeist Yves Bourhis, triple jumper Sally Sarr and Amadou Dia Ba, Senegal's first and, to date, only Olympic medalist. As the Olympic cauldron was lit, dancers wearing masks and futuristic costumes created a pathway for an Afrofuturism-inspired fashion show. The act also featured a standout performance by a 12-year-old drummer whose solo drew loud applause. At 8:30 p.m., the performers took their final bow, bringing the ceremony to a jubilant close. Held in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly from Oct. 31 to Nov. 13, the fourth edition of the YOG will bring together more than 2,600 athletes from over 200 delegations. A total of 25 sports will feature on the official competition program, alongside 10 engagement sports. Dakar 2026 will also feature the Youth Olympic debuts of wushu, baseball5 and skateboarding, as well as the Refugee Olympic Team's historic first appearance at the Games. China has sent 66 athletes to compete in 21 sports at the Dakar Youth Olympics. Wushu athlete Lin Yilei and swimmer Chang Mohan, both 15, were named China's flagbearers for the opening ceremony. item.title: China's "porcelain capital" wins Global Award for Sustainable Development in Cities
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01
China's "porcelain capital" wins Global Award for Sustainable Development in Cities This file photo shows a view of the Taoyangli Historical and Cultural Block in Jingdezhen, east China's Jiangxi Province. (Xinhua) FUZHOU, Oct. 31 (Xinhua) -- The global observance of 2026 World Cities Day was held on Saturday in east China's Fuzhou, with five cities, including China's "porcelain capital" Jingdezhen, honored with the fourth-cycle Global Award for Sustainable Development in Cities, also known as the Shanghai Award. The event runs from Oct. 31 to Nov. 2. Apart from Jingdezhen, the other four recipients of the Shanghai Award, which recognizes cities for achievements in sustainable urban development, are Addis Ababa in Ethiopia, Santiago de Cali in Colombia, Istanbul in Türkiye, and Katowice in Poland. The event brings together senior United Nations officials alongside representatives from national governments, local authorities, international organizations, academic institutions, the private sector, and community networks to share best practices and advance practical solutions to common urban challenges. In December 2013, the 68th United Nations General Assembly adopted a resolution designating Oct. 31 as World Cities Day starting in 2014. It was the first international day proposed by the Chinese government at the United Nations. Ceramic culture has long been an ideal medium for cross-civilization dialogue. As a cornerstone commodity of the ancient Silk Road, Jingdezhen porcelain was a defining cultural symbol, through which the world came to know China and China reached out to the world. Building on this legacy, Jingdezhen has embraced a model of development that combines cultural preservation with creative renewal. Former porcelain factories have been reimagined as cultural and creative districts, old streets are lined with ceramic-themed installations, and historic neighborhoods have been carefully preserved and revitalized. The city is home to more than 3,200 inheritors of intangible cultural heritage in ceramic craftsmanship. It has also been named in the UNESCO Creative Cities Network as a City of Crafts and Folk Art. Jingdezhen's recognition is just one example of China's broader urban renewal efforts. Urban renewal also holds huge potential for investment and consumption. China has set a target of renovating 1,500 old streets and factory compounds from 2026 to 2030, bringing in new industries and business models to inject fresh momentum into urban development. "Converting old streets and factory sites into cultural and creative districts drives growth in dining, retail and entertainment," said Yan Yuejin, deputy director of the E-house China R&D Institute. item.title: China unveils detailed plan for manned moon landing
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01
China unveils detailed plan for manned moon landing BEIJING, Oct. 31 (Xinhua) -- China will adopt a "two launches, lunar orbit rendezvous" architecture for its manned lunar exploration program, a senior engineer said on Saturday, as development work for lunar landing advances steadily. Wang Xiang, deputy chief designer of China's manned space program and chief designer of the lunar exploration program, outlined the plan at the 7th Manned Space Symposium in Beijing. Under the scheme, two rockets would separately send the Lanyue lunar lander and Mengzhou crewed spaceship into the Earth-moon transfer orbit, and the two spacecraft would perform a rendezvous and docking in the lunar orbit. Astronauts would then transfer from the Mengzhou spaceship into the Lanyue lander for the descent to the lunar surface and subsequent scientific work. Wang said the approach matches China's existing technical capabilities and infrastructure, and the separate development of the spaceship and lunar lander can help standardize production and support the formation of a long-term family of vehicles. While the plan also presents considerable challenges, Wang said the new system for mobilizing resources nationwide is the fundamental advantage for addressing them. He said the program has established system plans, technical standards and quality requirements under a single development framework, and has adopted an integrated design approach with emphasis on interface verification between subsystems. So far, the development of the Long March-10 carrier rocket, the Mengzhou crewed spaceship and the Lanyue lunar lander has been progressing smoothly. Major tests already completed include the Mengzhou spaceship's zero-height abort and maximum dynamic pressure escape tests, the Lanyue lander's landing and takeoff test, plus the low-altitude demonstration and validation test for the Long March-10 rocket. Wang said future lunar exploration should follow the principle of building knowledge and capability before moving into resource utilization, with a prolonged survey phase needed to understand the moon in a steady, step-by-step manner. He added that manned lunar landing and unmanned lunar exploration share many common elements in key technologies, infrastructure and personnel, and that achievements from the Chang'e lunar exploration program will also support the manned landing effort. item.title: Overseas observers say CPC plenum shows firm resolve in full and rigorous Party self-governance
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01
Overseas observers say CPC plenum shows firm resolve in full and rigorous Party self-governance The fifth plenary session of the 20th Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee is presided over by the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee in Beijing, capital of China. The 20th CPC Central Committee held its fifth plenary session in Beijing from Oct. 26 to Oct. 29, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhai Jianlan) BEIJING, Oct. 31 (Xinhua) -- The fifth plenary session of the 20th Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee concluded Thursday in Beijing after adopting a resolution on persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance. Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, delivered an important address at the session. The plenum made systematic plans for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, demonstrating the Party's resolve to strengthen its governing capacity, maintain its advanced nature and integrity, and keep close ties with the people, overseas political analysts have said. They commended the Party's sustained efforts to improve governance and combat corruption, noting that the measures would help translate long-term development goals into effective action, consolidate public trust and provide useful insights for other countries seeking stronger institutions and better public services. STRENGTHENING CAPACITY TO DELIVER The session stressed that strict management of officials is the key to full and rigorous Party self-governance. It called for implementing the Party's organizational line for the new era and applying stringent standards to the education, cultivation, selection, appointment, management, and oversight of officials. It also emphasized that Party organizations at all levels play the principal role in exercising full and rigorous Party self-governance, calling for systematically advancing their development at all levels and in all sectors to strengthen their political and organizational functions. For Lyazid Benhami, an expert on China-France relations, full and rigorous Party self-governance helps improve policy consistency, clarify officials' responsibilities and strengthen coordination across different levels of decision-making, all of which are particularly important in a country as large and diverse as China. An aerial drone photo taken on Nov. 2, 2025 shows the Three Gorges Dam and its outbound power transmission lines in Yichang, central China's Hubei Province. (Photo by Zheng Jiayu/Xinhua) For China, continuity in major strategic directions helps advance projects that require substantial investment and a long time to complete, he said. Combining that continuity with regular assessments of implementation enables the Party to listen to the public and adjust policies when necessary, Benhami added. Ling Tek Soon, senior lecturer at the Institute of China Studies of the University of Malaya, said the CPC's efforts to address its own problems and combat corruption reflect a long-term vision for governance. By continually improving the overall quality of its officials, the Party also creates room for fresh talent and ideas, he added. Joseph Mutaboba, a former Rwandan diplomat, highlighted the importance of connecting leadership, institutional responsibility and implementation. "Effective governance begins with the quality, integrity and accountability of public officials," he said. Merit-based recruitment, continuous professional development, performance evaluation, and transparent accountability mechanisms are essential for strengthening public institutions, Mutaboba added. BUILDING INTEGRITY, PUBLIC TRUST The CPC has outlined four areas of focus for steadfastly following a distinctive Chinese path to combating corruption, including maintaining a tough stance against corruption, strengthening checks on and oversight over the exercise of power, fortifying the cultural-ethical foundations for championing integrity and disdaining corruption, and enhancing coordinated efforts to prevent corruption by rooting out audacity, opportunity and desire. Eduardo Regalado, a researcher at Cuba's International Policy Research Center, said the approach addresses different causes of corruption: deterrence raises the cost of wrongdoing, institutional safeguards close loopholes, and education makes integrity an internal commitment. People visit an exhibition hall themed on integrity culture in Huzhou, east China's Zhejiang Province, Oct. 21, 2026. (Photo by Yi Fan/Xinhua) He also viewed the central Party leadership's eight-point decision on improving work conduct as an institutional means of curbing undesirable practices and maintaining close ties with the people. "Strengthening Party regulations and institutions turns political will into stable, predictable and binding rules and procedures," Regalado said, adding that this helps make full and rigorous Party self-governance sustainable and consistent with the modernization of national governance. Koh King Kee, president of the Center for New Inclusive Asia, a Malaysian think tank, said the anti-corruption campaign had sent a clear message that no area or individual was exempt from scrutiny. Effective supervision of power, sound institutions and education must advance together so that people experience fairness and justice in their daily lives, Koh said. Alberto Moreno, president of the Communist Party of Peru (Red Fatherland), linked the Party's long-term governing capacity to its ability to prevent corruption, bureaucracy and privilege from weakening its relationship with the people. "The CPC draws its strength from the people and always serves the people," he said. Institutional restraints and ideological education are inseparable, Moreno added, stressing the importance of combining discipline with officials' morality and commitment to public service. SHARING EXPERIENCE The endeavors to advance full and rigorous Party self-governance in the new era have broken new ground in the self-reform of the century-old Party and brought about historic achievements and transformations in the cause of the Party and the country, according to a communique issued following the plenum on Thursday. A participant reads a single-volume copy of the Kyrgyz and Russian versions of a think tank report titled "Contemporary Features and Global Significance of Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building" at the 2026 Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Media and Think Tank Summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, July 27, 2026. (Xinhua/Feng Kaihua) Such progress in self-reform has drawn praise from observers who see the ability to learn and adapt as essential to a governing party's long-term vitality. Peter Hediger, a Swiss sinologist, said the CPC's experience demonstrates an ongoing process of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of the times. "It is the dynamic nature of the CPC which has enabled pragmatic approaches to various political, social, and economic problems," Hediger said. Winston Alarcon, general secretary of the Communist Party of Ecuador, said Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building draws on Marxist theory while responding to China's national conditions, providing guidance for Party development and the country's modernization. The concepts of full and rigorous Party self-governance and self-reform have enriched Marxist thinking on party building, he said. For Latin American societies, an important lesson is the need to study their own history and culture, confront new challenges and develop theories grounded in experience, Alarcon added. Countries should explore independent development paths suited to their circumstances, he noted. Benhami likewise emphasized the wider relevance of combining strategic continuity with self-improvement. Countries with different histories and institutions can draw on that experience as they seek more accountable and effective governance to ensure that public resources serve the public interest and the benefits of development reach the people, he said. item.title: Political party leaders worldwide laud 5th plenary session of 20th CPC Central Committee
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01
Political party leaders worldwide laud 5th plenary session of 20th CPC Central Committee BEIJING, Oct. 31 (Xinhua) -- Leaders of political parties around the world have extended congratulations on the successful convening of the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC). They spoke highly of the CPC's experience and achievements in persistently advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance, and highly appreciated the important insights that Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building offers for the development of political parties around the world. Abhisit Vejjajiva, leader of Thailand's Democrat Party and former Thai prime minister, said that the CPC has accurately grasped major trends in global development and responded to the fundamental demands of the people. The CPC's governance practices and valuable experience offer valuable lessons and are worthy of serious reflection by other political parties, he said. Madhav Kumar Nepal, co-coordinator of the Nepali Communist Party and former Nepali prime minister, said Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building has answered questions that all political parties must confront but few have seriously addressed. Only by consistently attaching great importance to party building and having the courage to renew itself can a political party lead a country toward lasting peace and stability, he said. Luther Tarpeh, national chairman of the Unity Party of Liberia, said the CPC's successful governance model has paved the way for national rejuvenation with sustainable development, offering valuable lessons for the Global South countries. Sophia Shaningwa, secretary general of Namibia's South West Africa People's Organization (SWAPO) party, said that Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, has offered an effective solution to address the issue of party governance. SWAPO is willing to enhance exchanges and mutual learning with the CPC, and systematically study Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building, she said. Asha-Rose Migiro, secretary-general of Tanzania's Chama Cha Mapinduzi party, said that this meeting will consolidate the institutional foundation for Chinese modernization and the successful implementation of the 15th Five-Year Plan for National Economic and Social Development. Richard Todwong, secretary-general of Uganda's National Resistance Movement, said the CPC's efforts to strengthen party building have provided strong support for realizing Chinese modernization while offering a valuable model for developing countries, including those in Africa, to enhance their governance capacity. Dmitry Novikov, deputy chairman of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of the Russian Federation and first deputy chairman of the State Duma Committee on International Affairs, said what makes the CPC great is its ability to engage in self-reflection, face problems head-on and take action to address them, which ensures that power is exercised to serve the people rather than private interests and that the party maintains vitality and dynamism. In doing so, the CPC has set an example for political parties in other countries, he said. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Peng Liyuan chats over tea with wife of German president
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-31
Peng Liyuan chats over tea with wife of German president Peng Liyuan, wife of Chinese President Xi Jinping, chats over tea with Elke Budenbender, wife of German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 30, 2026. Budenbender is accompanying her husband who is on a state visit to China. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) BEIJING, Oct. 30 (Xinhua) -- Peng Liyuan, wife of Chinese President Xi Jinping, chatted over tea with Elke Budenbender, wife of German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, in Beijing on Friday. Budenbender is accompanying her husband who is on a state visit to China until Oct. 31. Peng happily recalled her trip accompanying President Xi on his visit to Germany in 2017 and expressed her appreciation for Budenbender's long-standing commitment to safeguarding the rights and interests of women and children. They watched a short film on the cultural and people-to-people exchanges between China and Germany. Peng noted that the cooperation between China and Germany in areas such as education and culture is rich and diverse. She expressed the hope that the people from both countries will maintain frequent exchanges, continuously enhance mutual understanding, and promote closer bonds between the two peoples. Budenbender expressed heartfelt gratitude for Peng's hospitality and her appreciation for Peng's work on cultural and people-to-people exchanges between Germany and China. She stated her willingness to contribute to deepening bilateral cooperation in relevant fields and enhancing friendship between the two peoples. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Xi meets president of Swiss Confederation, calling for more certainty for China-Europe economic, trade cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30
Xi meets president of Swiss Confederation, calling for more certainty for China-Europe economic, trade cooperation Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with President of the Swiss Confederation Guy Parmelin, who is paying a working visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) BEIJING, Oct. 30 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping met with President of the Swiss Confederation Guy Parmelin in Beijing on Friday, calling on both countries to inject confidence and more certainty into China-Europe economic and trade cooperation as well as into the global economic development. Noting Switzerland is an important partner of China in Europe, Xi said Swiss cooperation with China has always been at the forefront among European countries. He added that free trade cooperation has become the brightest highlight of China-Switzerland relations, which fully demonstrates the political courage and responsibility of the two countries in adhering to open cooperation, and highlights the unique leading role of both sides in promoting the building of an open world economy. China is willing to work with Switzerland to uphold openness, strengthen cooperation, promote a universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization, and jointly inject confidence and more certainty into the economic and trade cooperation between China and European countries, as well as into the global economic development, Xi said. Since the establishment of diplomatic ties, China and Switzerland have continuously translated the China-Switzerland cooperation spirit, featuring equality, innovation and win-win results, into pragmatic outcomes, setting a model for interactions between countries of different sizes and with different social systems, Xi pointed out. He said the two sides should respect each other, treat each other as equals, and comprehensively enhance exchanges and policy alignment at different levels. Noting that China is accelerating the development of new quality productive forces and steadily expanding institutional opening up, Xi said the country is ready to turn its market into a market for the world and a shared market for all. Both sides should adhere to mutual benefit and win-win results, strengthen innovation cooperation and focus on fostering cooperation in emerging industries, including digital economy, green energy storage and artificial intelligence, he added. Xi expressed hope that Switzerland would leverage its unique influence to actively promote balanced and stable development of trade between China and European countries. As China and Switzerland share similar positions and concepts in supporting multilateralism, Xi said both sides should deepen multilateral coordination and mutual support, firmly uphold the international system with the United Nations at its core and the international order based on international law, reform and improve the global governance system, and advance the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. Parmelin said that since the establishment of diplomatic relations, Switzerland and China have always respected each other, maintained close high-level exchanges, and achieved fruitful cooperation results in many fields such as trade and investment, scientific research and innovation, and employment. Noting that this year marks the 10th anniversary of the establishment of Switzerland-China innovative strategic partnership, Parmelin said that the two sides have successfully completed negotiations on signing a protocol on upgrading free trade agreement in a short period of time with high quality, demonstrating a high level of mutual trust between the two sides, which will inject new impetus into bilateral relations. Switzerland firmly adheres to the one-China policy and looks forward to strengthening dialogue and exchanges with China, upholding mutually beneficial cooperation, and promoting greater development in cooperation in various fields, he said. The Swiss side attaches great importance to the positive role played by China in international affairs and is willing to closely coordinate with China, adhere to multilateralism, safeguard free trade, and contribute to world development, prosperity, peace and stability, Parmelin added. After their meeting, the two leaders witnessed the signing of the protocol on upgrading free trade agreement and multiple cooperation documents in areas like scientific research, employment and the media. item.title: Xi holds talks with German president, calls for opening new chapter in all-round strategic partnership
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30
Xi holds talks with German president, calls for opening new chapter in all-round strategic partnership Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan pose for a group photo with German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier and his wife Elke Budenbender prior to the talks between Xi and Steinmeier at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 30, 2026. Xi held talks with Steinmeier, who is on a state visit to China, in Beijing on Friday. (Xinhua/Shen Hong) BEIJING, Oct. 30 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping held talks with German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier in Beijing on Friday, saying China is ready to work with Germany to open a new chapter in China-Germany all-round strategic partnership and promote the building of a more just and equitable global governance system. Xi said as the world's second and third largest economies, China and Germany bear significant responsibilities for the development of China-EU relations and the stable growth of the world economy. Xi called on both sides to enhance communication and collaboration, create a new model of cooperation featuring equality, mutual benefit and strategic stability, and send out positive signals to the world of choosing openness over isolation and cooperation over confrontation. China's policy toward Germany is consistent, stable and predictable, and China is happy to see Germany play a greater role in European and international affairs, Xi said, noting that China has attached great importance to Germany's status as a major country and always supported its reunification and development. Xi expressed hope that Germany will view China's development and its cooperation with China with an open and positive attitude, uphold a rational, pragmatic and friendly policy toward China, and adhere to mutual respect and equal treatment, which is a valuable piece of experience for the sustained and sound development of China-Germany relations. Noting that Germany is a representative of advanced manufacturing and high-quality products, while China is advancing its modernization through high-quality development, Xi said the two sides have compatible development strategies and broad space for cooperation. Xi said China welcomes enterprises from Germany and other countries to deepen their presence in China and share the benefit of its supersized market. It is hoped that the German side will provide a fair, transparent and non-discriminatory business environment for Chinese enterprises operating in Germany, he added. Xi expressed China's willingness to cooperate with Germany in areas such as artificial intelligence, green and low-carbon development, trade in services and digital economy to jointly enhance future competitiveness. Both sides should support cultural, educational and artistic exchanges, facilitate personnel exchanges, foster people-to-people connectivity, and create a favorable atmosphere for celebrating the 55th anniversary of bilateral ties next year, Xi said. China has always viewed the EU as a partner, and is committed to developing China-EU relations with sincerity and goodwill, said Xi, adding that history and reality have repeatedly shown that for China and the EU, cooperation outweighs competition and consensus outweighs differences. He added that as long as both China and the EU stay committed to the positioning of their partnership and maintain the tone of equal-footed dialogue, differences and problems can be resolved and will not hinder further development of China-EU relations. It is hoped that the EU will work with China in the same direction to jointly advance an equal and orderly multipolar world and a universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization, Xi said. Xi briefed Steinmeier on the fifth plenary session of the 20th Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, adding that the CPC is willing to exchange governance experience with major political parties around the world, including those in Germany. Steinmeier, who is on a state visit to China, said that over the past 25 years, he has visited China eight times. Hailing China's rapid development, Steinmeier said China has become a major country with considerable political influence as well as economic, scientific and technological strength. Germany greatly admires the tremendous development achievements China has made under the leadership of President Xi, he noted. Germany firmly adheres to the one-China policy and is fully confident about the prospects of bilateral relations, Steinmeier said. The two countries can properly resolve economic and trade differences via dialogue and consultation to achieve win-win results, setting an example for the world, he said. Noting that the international order is under strain, and the world expects China to play a bigger role, Steinmeier said Germany is ready to jointly shoulder the responsibility of safeguarding world peace and development with China, uphold the purposes and principles of the UN Charter and the authority of international law, support free trade and WTO rules, and oppose protectionism and trade wars. Prior to the talks, Xi and his wife Peng Liyuan held a welcoming ceremony for Steinmeier and his wife Elke Büdenbender at the square outside the east entrance of the Great Hall of the People. Xi and Peng also held a welcoming banquet for Steinmeier and Büdenbender on Friday evening. Xi stresses Party self-governance to ensure CPC remains strong leadership core (Xinhua) 15:59, October 30, 2026 BEIJING, Oct. 30 (Xinhua) -- Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, stressed the need to persevere with full and rigorous Party self-governance to ensure that the CPC remains the strong leadership core in advancing socialism with Chinese characteristics. Xi made the remarks at a symposium on Aug. 21 to solicit opinions from non-Party personages on drafting the resolution of the CPC Central Committee on certain major issues concerning persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance. The resolution was adopted at the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the CPC, which concluded on Thursday in Beijing.
